# R315 — Xe b9 native Level Zero copy-stream interop safety/API audit

Date: 2026-10-13
Status: source-only. No tests, build, GPU/device, process, profiler, model, Git mutation, or cleanup were performed. This is not runtime qualification.

## Pin and decision

Reviewed pristine XeStrata b9 source at b9f00e9db7fd56decdd9930ee84049d980b904e4, chiefly src/core/device.cpp:240-301, include/strata/core/runtime.hpp:21-64, 77-104, src/core/gpu.cpp:128-145, 262-305, 363-410, and src/prefill/prefill.cpp:270-340, 1429-1503, 2174-2404. The available IntelLLVM v7.1.1 install headers were inspected at /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/MistVVK/XeStrata/.worktree/fix-xestrata-e32-host-handoff-20261011/.tools/intel-llvm-v711/install.

The copy-only queue path is plausibly compatible with current SYCL/Level Zero interop when it succeeds: runtime context/device match, imported handle is an immediate command list, its descriptor requests in-order execution, ownership is transferred to SYCL, and prefill uses that queue only for copies, event records, and barriers. Existing prefill dependencies preserve slot reuse and host-stager source lifetime across queues. Source review does not establish that the loaded adapter accepts the precise native handle on the target build, that queue-group discovery is reliable on the B570, that cross-queue dependencies work on the actual installed runtime, or that exceptions after native command-list creation are leak-free. Do not qualify or enable by default from this audit.

## Resource and ownership findings

At device.cpp:253-258, dlopen first requests RTLD_NOLOAD and then falls back to a normal load. Successful dlopen returns a reference that must be balanced with dlclose; this function never closes it. Repeated create_copy_stream() calls therefore leak loader references. Retain the library only across symbol lookup and synchronous Level Zero API calls, then close it with an RAII guard. SYCL's own backend remains responsible for its own loader reference.

At device.cpp:281-288, a successful zeCommandListCreateImmediate returns raw cl, then make_queue(...ownership::transfer...) is called. On successful construction, transfer ownership and Runtime's streams_ lifetime are coherent: destroy_stream drains and removes the queue; Runtime destructor drains all queues before list destruction. However, if constructing backend input, locking/list insertion, or make_queue throws after native creation but before SYCL has accepted ownership, no explicit zeCommandListDestroy(cl) runs. The ownership extension documents transferred ownership, but the inspected API does not make the exception boundary's ownership state explicit. Use a local RAII owner that destroys cl until make_queue has returned successfully and the queue is safely stored; disarm it only then. If list insertion can throw after queue construction, keep a local queue and ensure its destruction owns the handle before propagating.

Also, if the first eligible COPY-only group fails zeCommandListCreateImmediate, the loop breaks and falls back rather than trying later eligible groups (282). This is safe as a fallback but can miss a usable group; record the selected/fallback result and consider continue after a per-group create failure.

STRATA_COPY_ENGINE is sampled once in a function-static initializer (247-250), so toggling it inside one process does not switch modes after first call. A/B controls must use fresh processes or this setting must be changed to an explicit initialization-time option. Report whether the route actually selected a copy-only group; fallback runs are not copy-engine treatment.

## SYCL/Level Zero API compatibility

The code is compile-time guarded by availability of both Level Zero and Intel SYCL backend headers (device.cpp:10-16) and runtime guarded by the device backend. That is good portability containment; absent headers, CUDA/HIP, failed symbol resolution, absent group, or failed list creation select create_stream().

The inspected installed Intel level_zero.hpp specialization for make_queue at lines 126-145 detects a ze_command_list_handle_t, passes the immediate-list discriminator to the backend, uses the supplied context/device and ownership flag, and transfers ownership when requested. Intel's current backend extension describes this API as available for command lists from extension version 4 onward and warns that L0 v2 requires an in-order command list; the b9 descriptor explicitly requests ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_FLAG_IN_ORDER and the SYCL property queue::in_order. Verify the build's feature-test macro/adapter version at compile or startup, rather than assuming header availability implies a matching runtime adapter.

The runtime creates context_(device_) and extracts both device_ and context_ handles from those same objects (device.cpp:197-200, 259-260). That satisfies the required same-context/device association on source inspection. Do not substitute a device handle or context from another runtime/device.

The standard prefill edge pattern remains explicit:
- copy submission includes the slot's last-reader event via handler::depends_on (gpu.cpp:274-283; issuer at prefill.cpp:1476-1485);
- copied[slot] stores the resulting event; consumer compute queues call stream_wait_event (gpu.cpp:396-400, prefill around 2223/2359/2387);
- host stager calls event_record(dma_done, copy) before release-publishing issued (prefill.cpp:372-376), and its worker waits that event before overwriting the pinned ring buffer (331-338).
All queue/event objects originate from the same Runtime context. SYCL explicit event dependencies and queue barriers are the intended graph edges; in-order provides only within-queue order, so those cross-queue edges must not be removed.

The copy queue is documented as “events alone” and “No kernel may go on it” (runtime.hpp:47-49), but this is a comment rather than an enforced type/guard: gpu::launch, copy2d_async (implemented as parallel_for), memset, graph launch and host-task wrappers accept any engine stream (gpu.cpp:286-305, 316+, 358+, 415+, 504+; Runtime::stream only checks ownership). Current prefill use is copies/event/barrier only, but a later accidental kernel or graph call could send compute work to a copy-only engine and fail. Add a queue-role check or narrower copy-queue wrapper that rejects kernel/graph/host-task/memset operations; test the rejection.

## Profiling and synchronization caveats

The queue is created with only the in-order property (device.cpp:283-288), not enable_profiling. Event recording uses submit_profiling_tag when marks_by_barrier() is false (gpu.cpp:371-379). Intel's installed profiling-tag helper uses the device's native ext_oneapi_queue_profiling_tag aspect when present; otherwise it throws unless profiling was enabled on that queue (profiling_tag.hpp:18-38). Runtime normally measures tag-vs-barrier on a generic queue on the same device and catches unsupported tag submission, but STRATA_EVENT_MARK=tag bypasses that probe (device.cpp:209-231). In that forced mode, if the device lacks the native aspect, this imported queue also lacks enable_profiling and event recording can fail. This failure deserves explicit handling because Stager::issued_one ignores event_record's boolean result and advances issued (prefill.cpp:372-376), which would make the host ring believe a DMA completion was recorded. Before using the new queue, either reject forced tag mode without the native aspect, enable/verify queue profiling as appropriate, or make event_record failure stop publication and drain the possibly submitted copy before source reuse. Keep timing events/profiling out of the minimal correctness fixture unless separately qualified.

The copy queue must never be used for a host/device concurrent doorbell or polling protocol. The known B570 capability status for this work is host atomics unavailable; an engine queue or queue barrier does not provide host/device atomic synchronization. Keep the model's established CPU/GPU serialized handoff safety gate independent from this copy path.

## Fixes and minimum bounded validation before enablement

Before any performance A/B:
1. Balance dlopen with RAII dlclose; add RAII ownership for the immediate command list across every error/exception edge, with explicit transfer only after successful queue adoption.
2. Make STRATA_COPY_ENGINE initialization semantics explicit and log one of: off, copy-only queue selected (ordinal), or generic fallback with reason. Confirm the actual Level Zero runtime adapter supports imported in-order immediate lists; compile-time headers alone are insufficient.
3. Add an explicit copy-only queue role check preventing kernels, graph launches, host tasks, and memset/copy2D's parallel_for fallback from landing on this queue.
4. Handle per-group immediate-list creation failures by trying the next eligible group before generic fallback.
5. Make event-mark selection valid for the copy queue as described above.

Smallest useful GPU fixture (not run here): allocate a host-USM source and device-USM destination in the Runtime context; enqueue a copy on create_copy_stream, record its event, enqueue a compute-queue kernel that depends on that copy event and verifies bytes/canaries; then enqueue a second copy that depends on a compute-queue-produced event and verify that dependency too. Repeat with in-order/queue-drain teardown and injected pre-adoption failure if a small seam permits it. Test generic fallback and copy-only selection as separate cases, and reject kernel dispatch directly to the copy queue. A CPU-only fake/adapter-contract test should cover dlopen/dlsym failure, no copy-only group, immediate-list create failure for one group followed by another eligible group, and every throw point before/after make_queue adoption. This bounded fixture demonstrates compatibility/lifetime only; it does not qualify model polling or performance.

Related source-only work already recorded:

- research-native-copy-cohort-source-lifetime-review-round287-v1.txt — existing host-stager and copy-cohort lifetime/dependency conditions.
- research-native-copy2d-runtime-dispatch-safety-round291-v1.txt — separate memcpy2d dispatch/admission risk; not a substitute for this queue import audit.
- research-xe-b9-prefill-port-candidates-round310-v1.txt and research-current-prefill-measured-ledger-next-step-round313-v1.txt — performance candidate rankings; this report makes no throughput claim.
- Closed W report registry v175 at .../bench/results/2026-10-13-xe-b9-update/report-registry-v175.json indexes R309/R310 reports and states main-only test execution. It contains no runtime qualification for this specific create_copy_stream exception/ownership boundary.

Primary Intel references:

- Intel SYCL queue barrier extension: https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/supported/sycl_ext_oneapi_enqueue_barrier.asciidoc
- Intel SYCL profiling-tag header: https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/include/sycl/ext/oneapi/experimental/profiling_tag.hpp
- Level Zero specification repository: https://github.com/oneapi-src/level-zero

These API/source references support compatibility requirements, not successful operation or timing on this B570.
